```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

## Load the data

```{r load-data}
con = DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "../Data/midwest_airbnb_extended.db")
listings     = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "listings") |> tibble::as_tibble()
availability = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "availability_monthly") |> tibble::as_tibble()
reviews      = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "reviews_monthly") |> tibble::as_tibble()
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)

# Quick check: row counts should be 14,887 / 158,741 / 142,388
nrow(listings)
nrow(availability)
nrow(reviews)
```

## Task 1

```{r task1}
# Count how many listings each host has, across all three cities
host_counts = listings |>
  dplyr::count(host_id, name = "host_listings")

# Join that count back onto every listing
listings_hosts = listings |>
  dplyr::left_join(host_counts, by = "host_id")

# [A1] Number of hosts with 10 or more listings
host_counts |>
  dplyr::filter(host_listings >= 10) |>
  dplyr::summarize(hosts_10_plus = dplyr::n())

# [A2] (and B2): percent of each city's listings held by those hosts
listings_hosts |>
  dplyr::group_by(city) |>
  dplyr::summarize(pct_held_by_10plus_hosts = mean(host_listings >= 10) * 100)
```

## Task 2

```{r task2}
# Entire homes that sleep 4+, with 10+ reviews and a 4.8+ rating,
# then median price per person by city and neighbourhood
family_value = listings |>
  dplyr::filter(room_type == "Entire home/apt",
                accommodates >= 4,
                number_of_reviews >= 10,
                review_scores_rating >= 4.8) |>
  dplyr::mutate(price_per_person = price / accommodates) |>
  dplyr::group_by(city, neighbourhood) |>
  dplyr::summarize(median_price_per_person = median(price_per_person, na.rm = TRUE),
                   n_listings = dplyr::n(),
                   .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::filter(n_listings >= 20)

# [A3] Columbus neighbourhood with the lowest median price per person (top row)
family_value |>
  dplyr::filter(city == "Columbus") |>
  dplyr::arrange(median_price_per_person)
```

## Task 3

```{r task3}
# Median price, reviews per month, and estimated revenue
# by city and room type, in one summarize call
earnings = listings |>
  dplyr::group_by(city, room_type) |>
  dplyr::summarize(
    dplyr::across(c(price, reviews_per_month, estimated_revenue_l365d),
                  ~ median(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    n_listings = dplyr::n(),
    .groups = "drop")

earnings

# [A4] Median estimated revenue of Twin Cities entire homes
earnings |>
  dplyr::filter(city == "Twin Cities", room_type == "Entire home/apt") |>
  dplyr::select(city, room_type, estimated_revenue_l365d)
```

## Task 4

```{r task4}
# Within each city: sort by estimated revenue (largest first),
# mark the top 10 percent of rows, and compare their revenue to the city total
concentration = listings |>
  dplyr::group_by(city) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(estimated_revenue_l365d), .by_group = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::mutate(top_10pct = dplyr::row_number() <= ceiling(0.10 * dplyr::n())) |>
  dplyr::summarize(
    n_listings        = dplyr::n(),
    n_top             = sum(top_10pct),
    total_revenue     = sum(estimated_revenue_l365d, na.rm = TRUE),
    top_revenue       = sum(estimated_revenue_l365d[top_10pct], na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_revenue_top10 = top_revenue / total_revenue * 100)

# [A5] Columbus row, last column (and all three cities for B2)
concentration
```

## Task 5

```{r task5}
# October 2026 availability for entire homes only
entire_oct = listings |>
  dplyr::filter(room_type == "Entire home/apt") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(availability |> dplyr::filter(month == "2026-10"),
                    by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(mostly_taken = nights_available < 0.5 * nights_in_month)

# [A6] city with the lowest share (top row) and [A7] that share
entire_oct |>
  dplyr::group_by(city) |>
  dplyr::summarize(n_entire_homes     = dplyr::n(),
                   share_mostly_taken = mean(mostly_taken),
                   pct_mostly_taken   = mean(mostly_taken) * 100) |>
  dplyr::arrange(share_mostly_taken)
```

## Task 6

```{r task6}
# Attach each listing's city to its monthly reviews,
# keep July 2025 - June 2026, and total reviews per city and month
seasonal = reviews |>
  dplyr::inner_join(listings |> dplyr::select(id, city), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::filter(month >= "2025-07", month <= "2026-06") |>
  dplyr::group_by(city, month) |>
  dplyr::summarize(total_reviews = sum(reviews), .groups = "drop")

# Twin Cities months, busiest first
twin_seasonal = seasonal |>
  dplyr::filter(city == "Twin Cities") |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(total_reviews))
twin_seasonal

# [A8] busiest month and [A9] busiest-to-quietest ratio
twin_seasonal |>
  dplyr::summarize(busiest_month  = month[which.max(total_reviews)],
                   quietest_month = month[which.min(total_reviews)],
                   ratio          = max(total_reviews) / min(total_reviews))
```

## Task 7

```{r task7}
# Entire homes whose superhost status is known ("t" or "f", not NA)
superhost = listings |>
  dplyr::filter(room_type == "Entire home/apt",
                host_is_superhost %in% c("t", "f")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(city, host_is_superhost) |>
  dplyr::summarize(median_price  = median(price, na.rm = TRUE),
                   median_rating = median(review_scores_rating, na.rm = TRUE),
                   n_listings    = dplyr::n(),
                   .groups = "drop")
superhost

# Premium (for B1) = superhost median price minus other-host median price, per city
superhost |>
  dplyr::group_by(city) |>
  dplyr::summarize(
    superhost_price = median_price[host_is_superhost == "t"],
    other_price     = median_price[host_is_superhost == "f"],
    premium_dollars = superhost_price - other_price)
```

## Task 8

```{r task8}
# Listings with NO rows in the availability table
no_availability = listings |>
  dplyr::anti_join(availability, by = "id")

# [A10] How many listings the availability join loses
no_availability |>
  dplyr::summarize(n_lost = dplyr::n())

# Which city loses the most (for the README)
no_availability |>
  dplyr::count(city, sort = TRUE)
```
